claims.statement: OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution bare-earth digital terrain model with protruding features removed.
Grid and contour products are supplied as 10km by 10km tiles identified by the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
The Terrain 50 grid has regular 50m post spacing.
Each ASCII grid tile contains 200 rows and 200 pixels per row.
Height values represent the centre of each 50m pixel and rows run west to east from a north-west origin.
ASCII grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1m.
The grid supply includes ASC, GML, PRJ, auxiliary XML and per-tile metadata files.
GML provides location, grid spacing, vertical reference and spatial-reference metadata while the ASCII file carries the raster heights.
Per-tile processing date records tile creation by Ordnance Survey and is not the date of real-world survey or change.
Tile metadata distinguishes new imagery, partial revision and imagery examined with no change through lineage text.
GML identifiers are unique within a release but are regenerated when a whole tile is refreshed.
Terrain products use whole-tile refresh rather than feature-based change-only updates.
Terrain 50 GML expresses British National Grid using urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700.
Terrain 50 is available by online download without registration and the national tiled supply is arranged in 2,858 tiles.
No official TQ29 archive bytes, checksum, header or the two required candidate-cell height values were captured.
